correctness.rationale: At the assigned tree reconstructed RESULT.md and verify.py. For any m-ball of radius r and interior eccentricity s, the radial distance is -s(e.u)+sqrt(r^2-s^2+s^2(e.u)^2). The odd term integrates to zero. For m>=2 the square-root integrand decreases strictly with s on all directions other than the two poles, which have spherical measure zero. Thus the mean radial distance is strictly decreasing in s. For any affine hyperplane H through a and b in the ambient d-ball, its section is a (d-1)-ball centered at the perpendicular foot c_H, with common radius sqrt(R^2-|c_H|^2), and |x-c_H|^2=|x|^2-|c_H|^2. Hence the section and ambient comparisons have the identical radius ordering for all d>=3, including a=b. When d=2 its line-section sum is the constant chord length 2r, so the boundary exclusion is essential. The proof is pointwise and complete for all dimensions; the code’s numerical quadrature is only a regression check.
